We discovered that using the 4300 \angstrom \lambda_1 index instead of the 6302 \angstrom \ion{Ca}{II} line area reduced our error estimates for the solar radial velocity signal by approximately 30%. We found no benefit in using the 4000 \angstrom < 4300 \angstrom band and 6302 \angstrom < 6305 \angstrom feature combinations, and instead, they increased our error estimates. Furthermore, using a combination of these features

To differentiate between zero-energy peaks originating from Majorana and those from other causes at non-zero temperatures, we suggest tunneling spectroscopy as a method. This approach involves attaching resistive electrodes to a nanowire or island displaying a zero-energy peak. The varying temperatures at which the resistivity and tunneling conductance are measured allow us to determine the nature of the zero-energy peak. The idea is that if the peak represents a Majorana mode, it will remain unchanged by the attachment of the resistive electrodes, whereas if the peak does not represent a Majorana mode, it will be split and may disappear at higher temperatures due to the influence of the resistive contacts. The major roadblock to implementing this technique involves the nanoscale measurement of the resistivity of the electrodes. The proposed strategy could potentially be applied to currently-operating devices to confirm the existence of Majorana modes or to eliminate alternative explanations for zero-energy peaks.

The theory of shadows constitutes an axiomatic bicategorical framework, extending and matching key characteristics of topological Hochschild homology (THH), notably preserving properties akin to Morita invariance. Through the incorporation of Berman's extension of THH to bicategories, it is demonstrated that functors from the THH of a bicategory are equivalent to shadows of that bicategory, ultimately establishing a direct relationship between them. Furthermore, this connection serve as a basis for an intuitive proof of the invariance of shadows under Morita equivalence.

Existing approaches to image editing tasks like color grading often yield multiple possible outcomes rather than a single definitive result, as numerous different styles are applicable to these operations. Current machine learning-based methods typically disregard this stylistic variability in their pursuit of identifying a unique solution. Conversely, our research aims to harness style-specific information, extracting it from paired images to condense into a two or three-dimensional vector, resulting in a more efficient and understandable framework for style-based image editing. By representing the relationship between global color tones across paired images as a flow conditioned on the polynomial characteristics of the image pixels, our technique proves superior to other low-dimensional encoding methods, ultimately achieving accuracy rates nearly on par with state-of-the-art techniques and marking a notable improvement of 7 to 10 dB.

This technical report showcases the winning model of the AQTC task, recently introduced in the LOVEU challenge at CVPR 2022, where experts faced significant challenges in processing multi-step responses, multiple modalities, and dynamic button representations within video content. To overcome this, we developed a novel context-module that leverages deep features from both video and image confirmer components to enhance recognition. We also established a dataset with 2580 annotated instances from European VIDEO datasets and introduced an exclusive evaluation metric to measure performance. Our context-module-based model achieved a remarkable 88% average accuracy across three evaluation sets. Notably, this report documents the data creation process, submits three distinct models, and presents detailed training and testing procedures.

This field research focuses on snow deposition dynamics by monitoring the atmosphere's flow patterns and snowflake trajectories in real time. A state-of-the-art, high-resolution imaging system is utilized to capture snowflakes in motion, mapping the flow patterns and detecting vortex formations above the ground. Concurrently, a high-resolution camera is employed to track individual snowflakes in a smaller sample area within the main field of view, revealing the connection between atmospheric turbulence and snowflake settling patterns. Our research reveals that as snowflakes interact with turbulence at critical velocities, their falling speed is greatly increased, a phenomenon not seen in other studies. Images captured within the flow patterns show that snowflakes tend to concentrate near the base of vortex formations, moving preferentially downwards. High-resolution footage of these vortex formations provides quantitative evidence of accelerated snowflake speeds. This study provides comprehensive evidence that a phenomenon called preferential sweeping is the primary cause of enhanced snow deposition in the atmosphere's lower layers.

A fundamental theory known as active inference underpins how living beings interact with their surroundings. This theory views the brain as an efficient tool that employs Bayesian principles to create a detailed mental framework, aiming to minimize uncertainty about the world. While this framework has been successful in simulated settings, its application in real-world scenarios remains a challenge due to limited knowledge about the underlying statistics of the environment. This article presents a novel approach that addresses this issue by leveraging the capabilities of modern deep learning technologies. We have developed a deep active inference framework that can be trained end-to-end for autonomous robot navigation. Unlike existing solutions that often rely on hand-crafted representations and predictive models, our method can naturally discover more effective representations and predictions through self-improvement. We have conducted comprehensive experiments in diverse environments to evaluate our approach and compare its performance with state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our model can learn summary representations of its environment and utilize them to achieve high navigation efficiency, especially at a scale of seconds to minutes.

In experimental facilities specializing in high energy physics, nuclear physics, and cosmology, the task of processing large amounts of data in real-time is proving to be a substantial hurdle. As an alternative to standard compression methods, the use of machine learning algorithms has gained attention for real-time data reduction. Yet, data sets generated from scientific endeavors often comprise vast 3D data volumes characterized by significant portions of zeroes, non-uniform distribution of values, and high generation rates. Consequently, direct applications of standard compression methods are impractical. To address this issue, we introduce the Bicephalous Convolutional AutoEncoder (BCAE), a proprietary algorithm designed specifically for the efficient compression of such sparse 3D data volumes. By accounting for the inherent structure of the data in terms of spatial correlations, temporal dependencies, and depth relationships, the BCAE has demonstrated improved data reduction efficiency when compared to traditional methods.

Utilizing Finzi's gravity theory that enhances interactions at large scales, we analyze galaxy clusters from a thermodynamic perspective, establishing a statistical model and deriving thermodynamic equations in the process. We discuss the implications of a discrete energy state due to the theory's non-differentiable nature, along with the exothermic nature of interactions, marking the beginning of a new phase at a critical temperature. Our analysis includes an examination of the equation of state, specific heat capacity, and the relation between energy and number of particles, ultimately comparing our findings to numerical values from the Cannonball Model.

A type of convex geometric hypergraph, known as cgh, comprises a set of subsets originating from strictly convex point sets in the plane. In this study, researchers explore a specific type of problem associated with 3-element subsets called triangles. They identify a set of 11 distinct saturation problems for determining the maximum number of certain color occurrences in these subsets, given a specific color scheme. Similar to the challenges presented by Hadwiger's conjecture, solving all the identified problems would yield a comprehensive answer to a particular question regarding geometric hypergraphs. While some of these problems are proven to have a specific solution based on established theories, others are proven to have a specific solution based on established theories, while others remain unsolved and require further investigation.

To gain a better understanding of the relative contributions of different processes, the angular distributions and energy spectra of $\alpha$ and deuterons resulting from breakup, transfer, and incomplete fusion have been measured and calculated. Cross-sections for the production of $\alpha$ particles via different processes were found to be almost identical, indicating that the excitation energies of the resulting compound nuclei were primarily determined by the $\alpha$ particle energy. Further analysis showed that the angular distributions of the $\alpha$ particles and deuterons exhibited distinct patterns, with the $\alpha$ particles concentrating around the direction of the relative velocity between the two original nuclei, while the deuterons were found distributed equally around the forward and backward directions. A computational model, which accounts for the effects of Coulomb interaction and is based on the eikonal approximation, was able to reasonably reproduce the measured data, including the energy spectra and angular distributions. Additionally, the model was able to provide a quantitative breakdown of the cross-sections for the different processes involved, such as breakup, transfer, and incomplete fusion, which helped to validate the measured data and identify trends across varying nuclear parameters.

A previously overlooked ability in bio-inspired snake robots is dynamic vertical climbing. A novel locomotion technique mimicking the Pacific Lamprey's movement has been discovered, which enables a robot to navigate on flat surfaces while climbing at near-vertical inclines. A simplified model has been created to analyze the correlation between robot motion and actuation, resulting in the development of a new, adaptable robot inspired by the Pacific Lamprey. The new robot, called Trident, successfully demonstrates dynamic vertical climbing at speeds of up to 4.8 cm/s and can also move horizontally at 9 cm/s. Furthermore, its climbing strides can be 14% longer than the Pacific Lamprey's, making this innovative design a promising approach for robots navigating steep surfaces with limited support points.

This paper outlines a novel probabilistic framework designed to identify the most effective combinations of treatments in cases of colon cancer-induced immune response. An Itō stochastic process models the colon cancer dynamics, whose probabilistic evolution is governed by the Fokker-Planck equation. To identify optimal treatment combinations, an open-loop control optimization issue is proposed. Simulation results demonstrating the use of Doxorubicin chemotherapy and IL-2 immunotherapy validate the introduced framework.

Optimizing wireless Device-to-Device (D2D) communication success depends heavily on minimizing excessive interference through effective device scheduling. Traditional scheduling methods mainly prioritize maximizing throughput and fairness without considering the timeliness of received data. This paper presents a novel D2D link scheduling strategy that balances both Age of Information (AoI) and throughput by employing a packet replacement policy, which ensures fair link activation. Analytically derived expressions demonstrate how the network's overall AoI and throughput are affected under complex spatio-temporal interference. Furthermore, a neural network is designed to learn and predict the optimal scheduling strategy given the system's parameters, enabling fast decision-making. Numerical results show that this proposed scheduling method leads to substantial performance improvements over time. Additionally, the trained neural network achieves significant reductions in computation overhead compared to traditional method complexity.

Moffatt first discussed the concept of helicity in a fluid without viscosity in reference [25] and explored its preservation in the case of barotropic, compressible flow with smooth solutions. This paper demonstrates that weak solutions to this system in a specific mathematical space ensure the conservation of helicity. Additionally, similar results were found for both homogeneous incompressible Euler equations and the surface quasi-geostrophic equation.

The researchers in a particular study extended the solutions found in complex geometric optics to a related system of equations, which was initially investigated in contexts of electrical impedance tomography and the integrable Davey-Stewartson II equations, focusing particularly on the large spectral parameter $k$ in a specified domain of $\mathbb{C}$. They then verified that this large $|k|$ behavior aligns with certain predetermined asymptotic criteria specified in a different research paper ($\mathrm{arXiv:2203.00745}$).

Calculations involving the orbital dynamics of merging compact binary systems,
including higher-order effects of gravitational wave radiation, reveal that late-time
eccentricities of inspiraling binaries are typically underestimated by standard
models by up to 30 percent for heavy systems like 300-solar-mass binaries at
10 Hz, and less so for lighter binaries. By incorporating more refined equations,
a novel, accurate analytic formula for eccentricities at late times is formulated.
Furthermore, this model's results remain largely insensitive to the masses of the
binary components, and general relativistic effects, and the methodology can be
easily adapted for discovering binary neutron star systems and other objects.

A proposed innovation combines the benefits of X-ray free-electron laser oscillators (XFELOs) and the undulator taper technique to create a groundbreaking X-ray laser. This is made possible by using an XFELO to seed a free-electron laser (FEL) amplifier with a specially tailored electron beam. The unique characteristics of the beam allow for the tail to be within the gain bandwidth of XFELO, generating a lasing seed that's used for further amplification, while the leading part of the beam, outside XFELO's gain bandwidth, can still be utilized in the FEL amplifier. The suitability of naturally occurring "double-horn" beam current and residual energy chirp from a chicane compressor has also been identified. The outcome is potentially record-breaking levels of nearly terawatt X-ray pulses with superior shot-to-shot stability, paving the way for groundbreaking research across various fields.

Event identification is crucial for informed decision-making in graph data analysis systems.  Graph-based machine learning has made notable advancements lately, but detecting events in evolving networks still poses difficulties for current frameworks. Real-life occurrences typically involve sudden changes in network behavior patterns. Current methods for dynamic node representations are ineffective at capturing event-driven network changes.  To address these limitations, we propose a new approach, called DyGED, for recognizing events in evolving networks using a combination of temporal self-attention and structural awareness.  Through extensive testing with diverse datasets, we demonstrate that DyGED consistently outperforms alternative methods in accuracy, achieving up to an 8.5% improvement.  Notably, it also offers improved scalability, boosting run times by as much as 12.5 times.  Furthermore, we introduce a set of benchmarks, along with open-source code and dataset resources, enabling researchers to build upon our work and facilitate further research in this area.

The solutions of the Guderley problem involving an imploding shock wave in an ideal gas are examined, focusing on how a power law initial density distribution affects the accelerating shock. This is achieved through in-depth analysis of self-similar solutions and their similarity exponents under different symmetry conditions and varying parameters of adiabatic index and spatial density exponent. Moreover, we show how these theoretical solutions can be accurately reproduced in Lagrangian hydrodynamic simulations, thereby validating and verifying these codes for a range of scenarios.

The growing presence of artificial intelligence systems has led to a significant rise in the need for their explanations. Transparency and stakeholder trust are achieved by reducing the opacity of these systems through the provision of explanations. In this paper, we will explore the interconnection between explainable AI and requirements engineering. The challenges in the XAI field will be highlighted and solutions proposed, with a framework and future research directions on how requirements engineering can aid in addressing these difficulties.

Characterizing colorectal polyps histopathologically is crucial to personalize patient treatment and follow-up, ultimately reducing the risk of undetected invasive carcinomas. The process of polyp characterization involves examining tissue samples for malignancy and dysplasia using histological analysis. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved medical pattern recognition accuracy; however, training these models necessitates vast collections of annotated medical images. In this context, we've developed UniToPatho, an extensive dataset consisting of 9536 annotated H&E stained patches derived from 292 whole-slide images, designed for deep learning-based classification and grading of colorectal polyps and adenomas. This dataset serves as a resource for researchers tackling the complex task of automating colorectal polyp characterization.

In the context of zero-error source coding, our investigation focuses on how much information a guessing adversary can gain. The underlying source coding problem is equivalent to finding the minimum number of vertices in a specific graph that cover all vertices in the adversary's graph. Conversely, the adversary's ability to guess the source sequence is equivalent to finding the maximum independent set in their associated graph. We established that the adversary's maximum gain of information is related to the source's conditional entropy and further connected it to a maximum flow minimum cut paradigm in graph theory. This relationship holds for both deterministic and stochastic source sequences.

Deep learning-trained generative models can function as a prior in under-determined inverse problems such as generating images from limited measurements, like a sparse dataset. A new hierarchical generative model called MrSARP is introduced in this research, specifically designed for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image generation, to produce SAR images at various resolutions simultaneously. The MrSARP model is trained alongside a discriminator that assesses multiple-resolution images together to verify their realism, representing a target at various resolutions. The study demonstrates the applicability of the MrSARP deep generative model in retrieving high-resolution images from lower resolution images of the same target. The cost function of the model is modified to improve its ability to recover input parameters based on multiple-resolution images. The performance of the model is assessed using conventional super-resolution error metrics on simulated data and is compared with conventional up-sampling and image sharpening methods that utilize sparsity, which are found to be ineffective in this scenario.

A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm variant employs a combined quantum-classical strategy to achieve approximate solutions for complex optimization issues.  To optimize a quantum circuit's parameters, we utilize a Bayesian approach as an auxiliary routine, evaluating its efficiency in contrast with alternative global optimizers.  The proposed technique leads to considerable reductions in circuit access frequency, typically the costliest QAOA component.  The framework performs well even at slow circuit repetition rates and with minimal quantum circuit measurements, yielding a reliable energy estimate.  Moreover, we investigate how our approach handles noise during circuit operation, discovering that for short circuits it remains resistant to disturbances.  The outcome of these findings supports the use of the suggested method as an adaptable tool to exploit the mixed capabilities of QAOA within imperfect quantum devices.

A versatile method has been devised for determining the overlap area between two ellipses. The proposed approach relies on computing segment areas between the two ellipses, using a secant line that intersects each ellipse at given points. The Gauss-Green formula enables calculation of an ellipse sector area, with a triangle either added to or subtracted from this sector area to obtain the segment area. For calculating the overlap area of two ellipses, the areas of relevant sectors and polygons are combined. The algorithm identifies the intersection points of two general ellipses by utilizing Ferrari's quartic formula to solve a resulting polynomial formed by combining the two ellipse equations, allowing for handling all cases of intersection points, including none, one, two, three, or four points. The proposed method has been implemented in C and validated through numerous tests with diverse input ellipses, demonstrating its efficiency for applications involving multiple overlap area calculations in simulations.

Building upon the work by Wang et al. (2020) for reinforcement learning, we examine the continuous-time counterpart of Q-learning under the entropy-regularized exploratory process framework. To handle the collapse of the traditional Q-function in continuous time, we derive a first-order approximation and introduce the term "small q-function". The q-function has connections to both the instantaneous advantage rate function and the Hamiltonian. We develop a continuous-time "Q-learning" framework based on the q-function, separate from time discretization, by characterizing its relationship to value functions and stochastic processes via martingale conditions. We apply this theory to create actor-critic algorithms for solving reinforcement learning tasks, and our numerical tests show that these algorithms can outperform state-of-the-art methods.

Quantum magnets' property profiles, where magnetic principles govern the low-energy behavior, are usually described by semi-qualitative theories such as spin waves. However, such models may not always work and more accurate descriptions are needed. Researchers use quantum Monte Carlo simulations to study a more detailed Hubbard model on a triangular lattice and find that quantum fluctuations completely destroy long-range magnetic order in 2D at any density, but with increasing density, the nature of spin fluctuations changes. This ground state is then analyzed using a self-consistent spin-lattice model derived from a more detailed theory, confirming predictions made by a larger phase diagram theory.

Accurate vertebrae localization and identification are crucial in various medical applications related to spine disorder diagnosis and surgical planning. However, certain pathological variations (e.g., vertebral compression fractures, scoliosis, and vertebral fixation) and imaging conditions (e.g., limited visibility and metallic streak artifacts in CT scans) make this task quite challenging. To address these difficulties, this paper presents an advanced and precise method that leverages in-depth anatomical knowledge of the spine to aid in accurate vertebrae localization and identification. By employing a novel key point localization model, vertebrae center activation maps are generated, which are then adjusted using a newly developed rectification technique to minimize partial vertebral visibility issues. An anatomically-constrained optimization method, informed by spinewre-related anatomical characteristics, is also introduced to accurately determine the total number of vertebrae and correct any errors in vertebrae identification. Thorough validation on a large, diverse dataset consisting of 662 CT scans revealed that the proposed method surpasses the state-of-the-art performance in terms of localization accuracy and identification performance.

Stochastic thermodynamics leverages Markovian jump processes to simulate spontaneous changes between quantifiable microscopic states. The flow rates of physical processes are calculated from the anti-symmetric transition measures defined on the network of states. The statistical behavior of these flow rates can be represented by normalized cumulants. This study applies the mathematical and topological structure of Markovian models to demonstrate the gauge invariance of the normalized cumulant-generating function. By taking advantage of this invariance, we have developed a streamlined method for the practical calculation of asymptotic averages and correlation times across a wide range of stochastic thermodynamic models. The method involves a simple algorithm based on network imitations and path-sampling simulations, which we present in a companion paper.

This research examines relative quantum cohomology for specific types of singularity, particularly in the context of toric surfaces and double elliptic surfaces. It finds that under certain birational transformations, the relative quantum cohomology remains invariant for toric surfaces but not for double elliptic surfaces, revealing that this discrepancy stems from the presence of non-trivial effective classes. The study then introduces a birationally invariant version of the relative obstruction class and derives key equations governing this extension, along with an explicit validation of the obstruction class's invariance through mirror symmetry.

Two piezoelectric materials placed near each other can transfer energy across an intervening vacuum gap by transmitting acoustic waves. Our research provides a mathematical explanation for how this energy transfer occurs, and reveals that specific conditions allow for complete transmission of these waves. This finding holds true for materials of any shape or orientation and can be determined experimentally through measurement of surface properties. Furthermore, we analyzed the optimal energy transfer between identical zinc oxide crystals for various orientations and found a significant number of conditions that facilitate this energy transfer.

We explore a cutting-edge method for optically manipulating polariton condensates at a microscale, relying on highly coherent fluids of semiconductor-based light-emitting systems. Theoretical research indicates that modern spatial light manipulation technologies can be employed to redirect and concentrate these polariton condensates away from their initial sources of excitation. In our study, we specifically investigate the use of a miniature liquid crystal lens in conjunction with digital light-in-flight interferometry, enabling the creation of multiple microscale polariton waves that can be directed and fused into a single polariton condensate. This technique may lead to breakthroughs in polariton research, including the development of faster and more agile SQUID systems and faster phase-slipping and non-equilibrium dynamics in polariton systems.

The disintegrating exoplanet K2-22b displays erratic patterns in transit best attributed to a dissipating debris cloud, with the formation process of this debris still unknown. Analyzing grain size and sublimation rate is essential in comprehending the environment that contributes to planetary disintegration. In this study, dual photometric data obtained through the Large Binocular Telescope, with wavelengths of 0.48 and 2.1 microns, are presented during a period of reduced dust activity, revealing a refined upper limit of the planet's radius of approximately 4500 km. Medium-depth transit observations also suggest particle sizes ranging from 0.5 to 1 micron, suggesting extremely high mass loss rates of about 3e8 kg/s, coherent with hydrodynamic escape theories. In contrast, explosive volcanic eruptions or other mechanisms generating this activity would demand exceptional geological activity levels. Combining these results with the maximum possible planetary size, our findings estimate the remaining lifespan of the exoplanet at approximately 370 million years; conversely, incorporating predictions from hydrodynamical models yields a remarkably reduced lifespan of only 21 million years.

We develop a novel algebro-geometric approach to studying the Milnor fibration and establish a significant condition for holomorphic function deformations to maintain the Milnor fibration intact. In consequence, we derive a strategy to divide the space of polynomials with a specified degree into discrete, localized segments where the diffeomorphism of the Milnor fibration remains unchanged within each category.

Daany is an open-source, cross-platform C# library focused on data analytics and linear algebra. Designed for.NET environments, this tool facilitates data preparation, feature engineering, and other data transformation operations. Developed atop.NET Standard 2.1 and compatible with.NET Core 3.0+, Daany consists of multiple VS projects that can be easily installed as a NuGet package. At its core, Daany utilizes the DataFrame data structure, complemented by data science and linear algebra capabilities, including time series decomposition (SSA, STL, ARIMA) and optimization methods (SGD). The library also integrates matrix and vector operations, as well as data plotting functionality. Daany's implementation bears similarities to Python's Pandas library. This guide serves as a comprehensive developer manual, outlining Daany's features, functionality, and usage, as well as a listing of related papers.

I challenge the conventional view of Galileo's influence on science by suggesting that he struggled with mathematical proficiency. This perceived weakness drove him to focus on experimentation and empiricism,, which are now iconic features of the scientific method. By exploring Galileo's mathematical difficulties, I illustrate that they prompted him to emphasize observation over theoretical mathematics,, thereby paving the way for Baconian empiricism. His decision to underscore the interconnectedness of science and philosophy also reflects his acknowledgment of his own mathematical shortcomings. Ignoramus, the Latin phrase for "we are ignorant," becomes a fitting motto for Galileo's scientific endeavors. His legacy,, I argue, should be viewed through the lens of his mathematical challenges,, which, in turn, further solidify the link between the scientific revolution and the Renaissance humanism of the time.

The increasing popularity of Tsallis' thermodynamic framework is largely attributed to its capability to describe phenomena exhibiting anomalous thermal properties, which requires adherence to generalized thermal equilibrium. Our study focuses on examining non-Gaussian influences on Saha's ionization through the application of Tsallis statistics. We address this challenge by generalizing the number density with a non-Gaussian distribution based on Fermi-Dirac theory and then formulate the Saha equation for cosmological recombination. Our analysis reveals the impact of non-Gaussian behavior on standard recombination processes, which we illustrate with specific examples, emphasizing that Tsallis' thermodynamic framework offers valuable insights into the non-Gaussian effects of deuterium, lithium, and boron production during the recombination period. However, when considering the relativistic correction, the non-Gaussian influence becomes relatively minimal. We also analyze deuterium recombination by employing various values of the non-Gaussian parameter (q) and find that Tsallis' thermodynamic framework predicts a wider temperature interval for deuterium Lyman series transition than Gaussian statistics. Notably, when p = 0.75, the temperature interval is approximately 300 Ky old.

The analysis of magnetic reconnection, a collisionless process, necessitates complex, computationally intensive kinetic models, contrasting with more feasible fluid-based simulations. Our study utilizes the Magnetohydrodynamics with Adaptable Embedded Particle-in-Cell (MHD-AEPIC) model to investigate the interaction between two magnetic flux ropes. By embedding kinetic models into MHD simulations only in relevant areas, this novel model enables more efficient computation. The comparative study involves three scenarios: the MHD-AEPIC model, MHD simulations paired with fixed embedded PIC regions, and full PIC simulations. The examination of reconnection rates, magnetic island spacings, and ion dynamics within these scenarios indicates good agreement among the models, with notably large adaptable PIC regions required within the MHD domain to achieve such convergence.

This document provides a summary of the content from a course held at Stanford University in the spring of 2018.  The course brings together insights from cognitive neuroscience and systems neuroscience to create intelligent systems by combining human and machine intelligence.  The course uses a tangible example - a digital assistant that learns and evolves through ongoing conversations with an experienced software engineer while beginning as an effective analytical and problem-solving tool.  Over time, these intelligent assistants develop essential thinking strategies and learn to rely on intuition through lessons learned from their expert counterparts.  As a result, these intelligent assistants become capable of working side-by-side as equal partners - serving as cognitive enhancements and digital prostheses that help their human partners make informed decisions and access powerful computing tools more efficiently.
